tier_reason: First-party _bench.json from public harness code (DagorEngine prog/1stPartyLibs/quirrel/quirrel/bench/benchmarks.py plus the .nut workloads) with Squirrel 3.2 in every row; baselines' compiler and flags are stated (clang-cl LLVM 21.1.8 /O2 /MT) but the CPU is given only as CPUID 'Intel64 Family 6 Model 183 Stepping 1' (Raptor Lake generation, no SKU or clock) and Quirrel's own build is described only as 'jam -sConfig=rel' (clang, mimalloc) with no compiler version or flags, so it stops one step short of A.

corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark. The Quirrel binary is the shipped configuration with mimalloc, while the repo bench README says a CRT-heap build is up to 2x slower on table-sweep workloads (50k-table particles sweep 0.20s vs 0.11s), so part of the margin over the Squirrel 3.2 baseline (sq3-64.exe, upstream sources built with clang-cl /O2 /MT on the CRT heap) may be allocator rather than VM. Quirrel's own build is only described as 'jam -sConfig=rel' in prog/tools/sq (clang, mimalloc), with no compiler version or flags on the page. Quirrel loses to Lua 5.5.1 overall in its own table (geomean about 0.87x, faster in 3 of 13), to LuaJIT -joff (about 0.51x) and to Luau 0.735 (about 0.54x, faster only on particles-kinematics); against QuickJS-ng it wins about 1.56x over the 11 workloads QuickJS has rows for (queen and sort have none) but loses on 4 of them (all derived from page data). The daslang dasProfile README (borisbat/dasProfile, Quirrel 4.29.1 vs Lua 5.5.1, 16 interpreted tests) gives geomean 0.89x on Apple M1 Max and 0.94x on Ryzen 7 PRO 8700GE (derived from page data); that suite has no Squirrel column and comes from a Gaijin-affiliated project. The README claim 'equal performance to Lua' is therefore roughly true and the only clear win is over Squirrel 3.2 (about 1.28x geomean, faster in 12 of 13). CPU identified only as Intel Family 6 Model 183 Stepping 1 (Raptor Lake generation, SKU and clock not stated). Each cell is the fastest of 3 whole processes, each process reporting the best of 10-20 in-process iterations; the standalone repo is a batched mirror of the DagorEngine tree (latest batch v4.41.0 on 2026-09-16, the table labels Quirrel 4.38.0).

notes: All Squirrel 3.2, Lua 5.5.1, LuaJIT, QuickJS-ng numbers and the derived geomeans (1.283x vs Squirrel, 0.867x vs Lua, 0.513x vs LuaJIT -joff, 1.56x vs QuickJS-ng) check out against _bench.json; the record also omits Luau 0.735, which beats Quirrel at about 0.54x. Shortcoming: wins only against its own ancestor Squirrel 3.2 (about 1.28x geomean), slower than Lua 5.5.1, Luau and LuaJIT -joff, and the margin over Squirrel mixes in mimalloc vs the CRT heap. License MIT, 223 stars, last commit 2026-09-16 confirmed; dasProfile geomeans 0.892x/0.943x recomputed and match.

tier_reason: First-party README tables with public scripts (MJIT-benchmarks/compare.rb, optcarrot-compare.rb and the .rb workloads) and a named CPU (i3-7100), but only the JIT's C backend is specified (GCC 6.3.1 -O2, Clang 3.9.1 -O2); the compiler and flags used to build the MRI 2.0, base and rtl_mjit interpreter binaries themselves are never stated, so not A; no paper or independent run, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README 'Update: 15th June, 2017' wall-time speedup over MRI 2.0, geomean of 23 microbenchmarks: mjit (GCC 6.3.1 -O2) 6.18x, mjit-cl (Clang 3.9.1 -O2) 4.02x, rtl without JIT 1.39x, base MRI 2.5-dev 1.12x; against base that is about 5.5x (mjit) and 3.6x (mjit-cl). The 'while' row (387.29x for mjit) is an empty loop whose result is unused; without it the mjit geomean is about 5.1x over MRI 2.0 and 4.5x over base, and on the ten algorithmic benchmarks (fannk through bench) mjit is about 1.93x over MRI 2.0 and 1.74x over base (all derived from page data). Optcarrot 2000 frames: 28.96 FPS MRI 2.0, 39.43 FPS base, 78.22 FPS mjit (2.7x), 90.58 FPS mjit-cl (3.13x); default 180 frames: 82.06 FPS mjit (2.83x), 85.43 FPS mjit-cl (2.94x). Optcarrot against base about 1.98x (mjit) and 2.30x (mjit-cl) at 2000 frames (derived from page data). CPU-time geomean 5.55x (mjit) and 3.67x (mjit-cl) on the microbenchmarks; optcarrot CPU-time speedup only 1.45x to 1.53x.
corrections.caveats: Numbers are from June 2017 on a prototype branch, last commit 2017-09-29; the branch is not maintained. The headline 6.18x is against Ruby 2.0, an old baseline; against the 2.5-development trunk it is about 5.5x. The 'while' microbenchmark (387x for GCC mjit) times an empty while loop inside a method whose result is discarded, which GCC -O2 can remove entirely, so that row measures dead-loop elimination and skews the geomean (about 5.1x over MRI 2.0 without it; about 1.9x on the ten algorithmic benchmarks, derived from page data). Compiler and flags of the MRI 2.0, base and rtl_mjit interpreter builds are not stated (only the JIT's C compiler: GCC 6.3.1 -O2 or Clang 3.9.1 -O2). Optcarrot is the only real-program result: 2.7x to 3.13x over MRI 2.0, about 2x over base, and CPU-time gain only 1.45x to 1.53x. Benchmark scripts are in the branch under MJIT-benchmarks (compare.rb, optcarrot-compare.rb; minimum of 3 runs timed with /usr/bin/time, start-up included). Not the same as the MJIT later shipped in Ruby 2.6 to 3.2 or today's YJIT (ruby/ruby is listed separately for YJIT); vnmakarov/mir is already catalogued and is not duplicated here. License: Ruby's dual licence (BSD-2-Clause or the Ruby terms), per COPYING.

notes: Every number in the record matches the README; downgraded A to C because the interpreter builds' compiler and flags are unstated. Shortcomings: 2017 prototype branch (abandoned), headline geomean against Ruby 2.0 and inflated by the 387x empty 'while' loop that GCC -O2 eliminates (about 1.9x on the algorithmic benchmarks, about 2x on optcarrot vs base); optcarrot CPU-time gain is 1.45x to 1.53x, not 1.49x to 1.53x. Fork of ruby/ruby, 206 stars, last commit 2017-09-29 confirmed; distinct from the listed ruby/ruby (YJIT) entry.

tier_reason: First-party docs table (cinderx/website/docs/introduction.md) against a no-JIT CPython run; benchmark sources are public (cinderx/benchmarks/fannkuch.py, richards.py, nbody.py and their _static variants, runner.py) but no Python version, compiler, flags or CPU model (only 'Broadwell 2GHz') are given, so C.

corrections.baseline: CPython interpreter with no JIT ('Baseline CPython interpreter with no JIT compilation enabled'; Python version not stated, CinderX requires 3.14; the benchmarks README gets its baseline with CINDERJIT_DISABLE=1, i.e. CPython with CinderX loaded and the JIT off)
corrections.caveats: The current repo README and PyPI page contain no benchmark numbers. The only table is in cinderx/website/docs/introduction.md: three micro-benchmarks, Python version of the baseline not stated, no compiler or flags, CPU only described as Broadwell 2GHz, and the JIT is slower on Fannkuch (4.40s vs 4.24s). The Static and Static + Primitives columns run rewritten, type-annotated sources (fannkuch_static.py and similar files in cinderx/benchmarks), so their 7-12x ratios compare different programs against the untyped no-JIT run; plain CinderX JIT on unmodified code gives 0.96x to 1.76x. The benchmarks README produces its baseline with CINDERJIT_DISABLE=1 (CinderX loaded, JIT off), so the 'No JIT' column may not be a stock CPython build. The repo ships a benchmark harness (cinderx/benchmarks, including fastmark.py for the full pyperformance suite and runner.py) but no committed pyperformance results; I found no independent measurement of CinderX against CPython 3.14. Older first-party claims sit in the cinder/3.10 branch README.rst of facebookincubator/cinder: 'can achieve 1.5-4x speed improvements on many Python performance benchmarks' and 'Static Python plus Cinder JIT achieves 18x the performance of stock CPython on a typed version of the Richards benchmark'; those measured the old CPython 3.10 fork before the 3.11+ adaptive interpreter and are not CinderX-on-3.14 numbers. The same README reports Instagram gains of about 5% from immortal instances and about 5% from awaited-call optimisation, which are not JIT figures. The facebookincubator/cinder main page is now a CPython 3.14 fork (3.8k stars, PSF license) and no longer carries those claims. Docs call CinderX experimental for external users; PyPI 2026.10.5.0 requires Python >=3.14,<3.16.

notes: Table numbers and derived ratios match the docs page exactly (JIT 1.76x Richards, 1.34x nbody, 0.96x Fannkuch; Static + Primitives 7.2x/8.3x/12.6x). Overlap: facebookincubator/cinder is already verified in wave 12 (jits, B) and its caveats say the JIT and Static Python now live in cinderx; this is the maintained MIT successor rather than a wrapper, so consider a duplicate fold or a cross-reference rather than two independent entries. Shortcomings: three microbenchmarks only, JIT slower on Fannkuch, the big Static Python gains need rewritten typed code, no Python version, compiler or CPU model; MIT, 282 stars, last commit 2026-10-06 confirmed.
